Recently vowed not to attend certain events in person.

Maybe if they paid me.

It is just getting too long and too scripted.

Asking (forcing) everyone to conform, by asking them to wear certain color, or response to certain prompt.

Does this happen elsewhere?

In addition, TSA has more relaxed policy when compared to BYU Athletics.

No bags bigger than a fanny pack or sling bag.

Just medication, buy everything there I suppose.

---

Back in the day, one can dress as you wanted, not to confirm.

This is no longer an individualized participation

---

There are times when the sporting event is no longer a spectacle.

But a reflection of life.

Heroes and anti-heroes.

Struggles and disappointments.

Triumphs and losses.

---

Here’s a cinematic version — with pacing, rhythm, and visual punch suited for narration or video:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

There are moments when the game…\

is no longer just a game.

It becomes something more.\

A reflection of life itself.

Heroes rise.\

Villains chase.\

There’s struggle. Disappointment.\

Triumph… and loss.

A runner breaks free—25 yards from glory.\

Opponents close in at 20.\

He shrugs off one… two… a third defender.\

Leaps over another near the 13.

Then—impact.\

Two defenders hit him at the 5.\

But here they come—five teammates, charging in.\

Together, they drive him forward.

Across the line.\

A defender still hanging on his leg.\

He hops into the end zone.

And in that moment—\

you realize...\

this isn’t just football.

It’s life.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A certain runner takes off 25 yards from the target.

Met by opponents, starting at 20 yards.

shakes off a third of defenders.

Jumps over another around 13 yard line.

Then 2 defenders jump on him at 5 yards.

This is when 5 of the offense joins in and pushes across the line, with a defender hanging onto the right lower leg.

That means he hopped to the end zone.

How similar is this to a life
